title: RASBU-SEPSIS Study: Effects of rasburicase on kidney during sepsis – a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial
official: RASBU-SEPSIS Study: Effects of rasburicase on renal function during sepsis – a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial
summary: Main objective: Determine the effect of Rasburicase on the occurrence and evolution of acute renal failure (ARF) in septic patients with uricemia ≥200 µmol/L.
conditions: Patients hospitalised in intensive care, diagnosed with sepsis less than 48 hours ago, uric acid level ≥200µmol/L, adults, negative G6PD deficiency

interventions.name: Fasturtec 1.5 mg/ml powder and solvent for concentrate for solution for infusion.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients ≥18 years old
2. Diagnosis of sepsis (presumed or known infection and increase in SOFA score ≥ 2), included within 48 hours of diagnosis.
3. Uricémia ≥ 200 µmol/L
4. Rapid diagnostic test strip for G6PD deficiency negative
5. Patient affiliated with a social security scheme
6. Informed consent form signed
7. Woman of childbearing age using effective contraception throughout the treatment and for 1 month after the end of the treatment.
8. Hospitalised in intensive care unit
Exclusion criteria:
1. Minor
2. Other metabolic disorders known to cause hemolytic anemia
3. Chronic treatment with a urate-lowering agent
4. Enrolled in another
5. Sepsis due to urinary obstruction
6. Surgery involving the kidneys or urinary tract in the last 3 months
7. Life expectancy less than 6 months
8. Pregnant or breastfeeding woman
9. Chronic kidney failure on hemodialysis
10. AKI with need for dialysis treatment estimated within 12 hours
11. Known hypersensitivity to Rasburicase, or to any of the excipients,
12. Pre-existing condition or situation at risk of lysis syndrome
13. Known G6PD deficiency or suggestive family history
